# GraphHelm community conduct

GraphHelm welcomes people who want to use, question, improve, or review the project. This policy applies to participation in this repository's issues, pull requests, reviews, and other project-managed spaces.

## Expected behavior

- Be respectful and specific. Critique an idea, claim, or patch without attacking its author.
- Make room for newcomers. Explain necessary context and accept good-faith questions.
- Keep reports reproducible and discussions on topic. Say what you observed and what remains uncertain.
- Protect privacy. Do not publish credentials, personal data, private conversations, or vulnerability details.

Harassment, threats, discrimination, sexualized attention, repeated personal attacks, doxxing, and deliberate disruption are not acceptable.

## Reporting and response

For abusive content on GitHub, use **Report content** on the issue, pull request, or comment. GitHub may offer a report to repository administrators or to GitHub Support, depending on the account and content. [GitHub explains those options](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github/reporting-abuse-or-spam). A GitHub Support report is handled by GitHub; it is not a confidential message to this project.

For a participation concern that is safe to discuss publicly, use the [question form](https://github.com/stabem/GraphHelm/issues/new/choose) and link the relevant thread. Do not put private evidence in a public issue. This project does not currently offer a separate confidential conduct-report inbox. A suspected software vulnerability belongs in the [private security reporting process](../SECURITY.md), not in a conduct issue.

The maintainer may ask for changes, hide or remove content, close or lock a thread, or restrict participation to protect the community. Responses should fit the behavior and its impact. GitHub controls any action it takes under its own policies. This document makes no promise of a private project investigation or response time that the project cannot yet support.
